question.text:
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING SETS IS/ARE COUNTABLE?

  • I. THE SET OF ALL REGULAR LANGUAGES OVER THE ALPHABET $\{0,1\}$.
     
  • II. THE SET OF ALL TURING MACHINES THAT HALT ON THE EMPTY STRING $\epsilon$.
     
  • III. THE SET OF ALL FUNCTIONS $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow\{0,1\}$.
     
  • IV. the set of irrational numbers $(\mathbb{R} \backslash \mathbb{Q})$.
     
  1. I AND II
     
  2. I AND III
     
  3. III AND IV
     
  4. I, II, AND IV
question.subject: Theory of Computation

question.text:
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING SETS IS/ARE UNCOUNTABLE?

  • I. THE SET OF ALL POLYNOMIALS WITH RATIONAL COEFFICIENTS.
     
  • II. THE SET OF ALL SUBSETS OF THE NATURAL NUMBERS $\mathbb{N}$.
     
  • III. THE SET OF ALL FUNCTIONS FROM $\{0,1\}$ TO THE SET OF NATURAL NUMBERS $\mathbb{N}$.
     
  • IV. THE SET OF ALL INFINITE-LENGTH BINARY STRINGS.
     
  1. I AND III
     
  2. II AND IV
     
  3. I, II, AND III
     
  4. IV ONLY

question.text:
Consider the following context-free grammar $G^{\prime}$, where $S, X$, and $Y$ are the variables (nonterminals), $0$ and $1$ are the terminal symbols, $S$ is the start variable, and the rules of $G^{\prime}$ are described as:

$S \rightarrow X 1 \mid 0 Y$

$X \rightarrow 00 X \mid 00$

$Y \rightarrow 11 Y \mid 11$
 

  1. $L\left(G^{\prime}\right)=\left\{0^n 1 \mid n \geq 1\right\} \cup\left\{01^{2 n} \mid n \geq 1\right\}$
     
  2. $L\left(G^{\prime}\right)=\left\{0^{2 n} 1 \mid n \geq 1\right\} \cup\left\{01^{2 n} \mid n \geq 1\right\}$
     
  3. $L\left(G^{\prime}\right)=\left\{0^{2 n} 1^{2 n} \mid n \geq 1\right\}$
     
  4. $L\left(G^{\prime}\right)=\left\{0^n 1^2 \mid n \geq 1\right\} \cup\left\{0^2 1^n \mid n \geq 1\right\}$

question.text:
CONSIDER THE FOLLOWING CONTEXT-FREE GRAMMAR $G$, WHERE $S, X, Y$ ARE THE VARIABLES, $a, b$ ARE THE TERMINAL SYMBOLS, AND $S$ IS THE START VARIABLE:

  • $S \rightarrow a X \mid Y b$
     
  • $X \rightarrow a X b \mid a b$
     
  • $Y \rightarrow a Y b \mid a b$
     

WHICH ONE OF THE FOLLOWING LANGUAGES IS GENERATED BY $G$ ?

  1. $\left\{a^n b^m \mid n \neq m, n \geq 1, m \geq 1\right\}$
     
  2. $\left\{a^{n+1} b^n \mid n \geq 1\right\} \cup\left\{a^n b^{n+1} \mid n \geq 1\right\}$
     
  3. $\left\{a^n b^n \mid n \geq 1\right\}$
     
  4. $\left\{a^{n+1} b^n \mid n \geq 0\right\} \cup\left\{a^n b^{n+1} \mid n \geq 0\right\}$
question.subject: Theory of Computation

question.text:
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING SETS IS/ARE UNCOUNTABLE?

  • I. THE SET OF ALL FINITE SUBSETS OF $\mathbb{Q}$ (THE SET OF RATIONAL NUMBERS).
     
  • II. THE SET OF ALL SUBSETS OF $\mathbb{R}$ (THE SET OF REAL NUMBERS).
     
  • III. THE SET OF ALL ORDERED PAIRS $(a, b)$ WHERE $a \in \mathbb{N}$ AND $b \in \mathbb{R}$.
     
  • IV. THE SET OF ALL ALGEBRAIC NUMBERS (NUMBERS THAT ARE A ROOT OF A NON-ZERO POLYNOMIAL WITH INTEGER COEFFICIENTS).
     
  1. I AND IV
     
  2. II AND III
     
  3. I, III, AND IV
     
  4. II ONLY
question.subject: Theory of Computation
